h1:
Mookata in Kamphaeng Phet
10 Best-Value Grill-and-Hotpot Buffets
intro: Once the heat eases off in Kamphaeng Phet, the dinner locals meet up for most is mookata — that domed Thai BBQ where one burner does both grilling and hotpot at the same time. You sit, talk for hours, and a couple hundred baht is enough to leave full. We picked the spots with real reviews behind them: places in town, the ones behind Rajabhat University, and a few out near Khlong Lan where you get the scenery thrown in too.

blocks.html: Most mookata in Kamphaeng Phet is a single-price buffet — sit and eat as much as you like, from traditional charcoal burners to combined grill-and-hotpot setups in air-conditioned rooms. The common ground at nearly every place: several marinades of pork, pork belly, grilled offal, meatballs, fresh vegetables, noodles, and a corner for desserts and ice cream. Where they differ is the freshness of the ingredients, the dipping sauces, and the vibe. We ranked them by the popularity and value that people in Kamphaeng Phet bring up most often.

blocks.text: 10 mookata and BBQ-buffet spots in Kamphaeng Phet

items.name: Sahai Jum Lang Mor
items.blurb: The one Kamphaeng Phet foodies talk about most. It's behind Kamphaeng Phet Rajabhat University, air-conditioned, clean, with long buffet lines of pork, beef, and seafood. You can do both grill and hotpot, and it's great for groups.
items.meta: Behind Kamphaeng Phet Rajabhat University · Open 15:00–23:00

items.name: Vintage Mookata
items.blurb: A newer, laid-back spot with vintage decor that photographs well. What people single out is the dipping sauce. It's behind Nawarat Hotel near the night market, so you can keep walking after dinner — good for couples or groups who want some atmosphere.
items.meta: Behind Nawarat Hotel, near the night market · Open daily 16:30–23:00

items.name: Phet Mookata
items.blurb: A long-standing mookata spot in town that reviewers say keeps a packed, varied spread — pork, chicken, seafood, fruit, and help-yourself desserts. Hot burners, always busy. Good for big eaters who want everything in one place.

items.name: Kirimatsu Shabu & Mookata, Kamphaeng Phet branch
items.blurb: A shabu-and-mookata chain people know by name. The Kamphaeng Phet branch is a timed buffet of roughly 2 hours, with both grill and shabu, an organized layout, and several dipping sauces. Good for families or larger groups.
items.meta: Kamphaeng Phet town · Timed buffet ~2 hrs

items.name: Shabu Moo Ood, Kamphaeng Phet branch
items.blurb: A Japanese-style shabu-and-grill spot. The single buffet price includes drinks and dessert, the ingredients are fresh and clean, and the seating is comfortable. Good if you love shabu but still want to grill some pork in the same meal.
items.price: Around 259 THB/person, drinks and dessert included

items.name: Kinza Buffet BBQ & Shabu
items.blurb: A grill-and-shabu buffet in town with pork, beef, and seafood on offer. Mid-range price, plenty of variety — good for a group that wants both grilling and hotpot under one roof.

items.name: Baan Rim Khlong Mookata
items.blurb: A canalside mookata spot that reviewers praise for both the setting and the flavor. Open-air seating with a cool breeze and a full standard spread — good if you want to escape the in-town places and sit back.
items.meta: Outside Kamphaeng Phet town · Open daily 16:00–22:00

items.name: Hangout Buffet Khlong Nam Lai
items.blurb: A favorite out near Khlong Lan–Khlong Nam Lai. Reviews say it covers everything — butter-grilled meats, grilled prawns, and a hotpot. Good if you're driving out to Khlong Lan and need a dinner spot outside the town center.
items.meta: Khlong Lan district (Khlong Nam Lai) · Dinner

items.name: Chom Na Mookata
items.blurb: A light-on-the-wallet buffet that reviewers call easy on the budget. The price includes free drink refills, and while the spread is modest it's good value. Good for couples or small groups watching the budget who still want all-you-can-eat.

items.name: Yang Ah Mookata Buffet 99
items.blurb: The cheapest in the list — 99 baht a head, plus 49 baht for drinks, so around 148 baht per person. All-you-can-eat with no time limit. It's in Soi Kamphaeng Phet 6, Yaek 7, and good for groups on a tight budget who want to sit a while.
items.meta: Soi Kamphaeng Phet 6, Yaek 7 · No time limit

blocks.title: How to pick your spot
blocks.html: If you're watching the budget, the cheaper spots like Chom Na and Yang Ah 99, or the zone behind the campus, start lower. If you want air-conditioning and a big spread, Sahai Jum behind the university and Kirimatsu both deliver. And if you're driving out to Khlong Lan, just stop at Hangout Buffet Khlong Nam Lai. Most places open around 15:00–16:30 and run late. Weekends get busy — go before 7pm or call to book.

blocks.text: How much does it cost, and is it worth it

blocks.html: Most mookata buffets in Kamphaeng Phet run 99–299 THB per person. Budget spots like Yang Ah 99 and Chom Na start around 99–149, while the in-town places with bigger spreads or the shabu-and-seafood spots climb to 259–299. If you eat a lot and stay a while, a buffet is clearly better value than ordering by the plate, and many places have no time limit. The thing to watch is that some add 7% VAT on top of the listed price.

items: Tight budget, 99–149 THB — Yang Ah 99 and Chom Na, good for watching the budget and for student groups
Mid-range, 199–259 THB — Vintage, Phet Mookata, Baan Rim Khlong, Hangout, with more variety plus atmosphere or seafood
Full spread, 259–299 THB — Sahai Jum behind the university, Kirimatsu, Shabu Moo Ood, Kinza, for air-conditioning, a big spread, or both grill and shabu

blocks.text: How to do mookata well and safely

items: Start by rubbing pork fat over the dome to grease it, then lay down the marinated pork — it won't stick to the burner.
Cook offal and seafood until they're genuinely done, especially the prawns and squid.
Keep separate tongs for raw and cooked food to cut the risk of an upset stomach.
Keep topping up the broth in the moat so you can blanch vegetables and noodles while the pork grills.
Save the desserts and ice cream for last, and take only what you'll finish so nothing goes to waste.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Prices and opening hours at each place shift with the season and promotions. Some add VAT or charge a fee for food you take but don't finish. Before you go, check the restaurant's page again or call to book a table on holidays — that's the safer bet.

faq.q: Which mookata in Kamphaeng Phet is the best value?
faq.a: If value is the priority, Yang Ah 99 comes to about 148 THB per person, all-you-can-eat with no time limit, and Chom Na starts around 149 THB with a modest but worthwhile spread. If you want air-conditioning and a big spread, Sahai Jum behind the university at around 279 THB is worth it in its own way.

faq.q: Roughly how much does mookata in Kamphaeng Phet cost?
faq.a: Most are single-price buffets in the 99–299 THB per person range. Budget spots start around 99–149 THB, while the in-town places with bigger spreads or the shabu-and-seafood spots run around 259–299 THB. Some add 7% VAT on top of the listed price.

faq.q: Is there a mookata spot behind the university in Kamphaeng Phet?
faq.a: Yes — Sahai Jum Lang Mor is behind Kamphaeng Phet Rajabhat University. It's an air-conditioned buffet with a big spread of pork, beef, and seafood, around 279 THB, open 15:00–23:00. Good for student groups and families.

faq.q: What time do mookata spots in Kamphaeng Phet open?
faq.a: Most open for dinner, starting around 15:00–16:30 and running until 9pm to 11pm depending on the place. Weekends get busy — go before 7pm or call ahead to book.

faq.q: Is there a mookata spot near Khlong Lan?
faq.a: Yes — Hangout Buffet Khlong Nam Lai, near Khlong Lan district. Reviews say it covers butter-grilled meats, grilled prawns, and a hotpot. Good if you're visiting Khlong Lan and need a dinner spot outside the town center.
